transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I keep losing track of what I’m supposed to be working on and can’t seem to stay organized with all the tickets and follow-ups at my job. It has started causing some major issues for me at work recently, which is why I decided to come in and get evaluated.
Can you tell me more about what you mean by 'losing track' of your work, is it that you forget instructions, have trouble sustaining focus, or something else?

It’s really a mix of things. I get easily pulled off-task by minor distractions like notifications or background noise, which leaves me with several half-finished tickets, and I struggle to prioritize them even with a mountain of sticky notes. On top of that, during longer calls or classes, my mind just slips away after about ten minutes and I realize I've missed chunks of what was said.
Have you been experiencing any significant feelings of anxiety, sadness, or emotional distress alongside these difficulties with focus and organization?

I haven't really been feeling significant sadness or anxiety, to be honest. It’s more just a lot of frustration and stress that directly comes from struggling to keep up with my work and being so disorganized lately.
Do you often find yourself fidgeting, feeling restless, or having an inability to stay seated for extended periods, especially in situations where you're expected to remain still?

Yes, I struggle with this constantly. On support calls, I'm always jiggling my leg, clicking my pen, or fiddling with things on my desk, and I usually don't even realize it until someone points it out. During long meetings or my three-hour evening classes, I get this pent-up energy where I feel desperate to get up and pace, just counting the minutes until I can stand.
Have these symptoms of inattention, disorganization, and restlessness been present since childhood, or did they develop more recently, perhaps around the time your work demands increased?

They've definitely become much more of a problem recently with my new work demands, but looking back, I've struggled with this since I was a kid. Back in elementary school, my teachers were always writing notes home about me daydreaming, blurting out answers, and never finishing worksheets. My parents still joke about how I could never sit still long enough to get through my homework without wandering off.
Can you describe how these symptoms have impacted your daily life and relationships across different settings, such as work, school, and social interactions, over the years?

At work, my disorganization recently led to a critical configuration error that caused client downtime, landing me on a formal performance improvement plan, and my evening class grades are slipping because I lose track of assignments. At home, it has strained my marriage because my wife is constantly frustrated with me for forgetting bills and errands. While these issues really peaked with my job's new fast-paced model, they've impacted my life in some form since I was a kid.

You mentioned these symptoms have been present since childhood but seem to have worsened with increased work demands; can you specify if there was ever a period in your life where you felt these symptoms were significantly less bothersome or well-managed?

Yes, before the last two years, things were much more manageable under my old work setup, which focused on longer, project-based tickets. I was able to rely on my natural style of deep-focus troubleshooting and late-night tinkering, which kept my difficulties from causing major problems. It wasn't until the recent shift to high-volume demands, along with mentoring and evening classes, that I really started struggling to keep up.

Can you tell me if you've ever had periods of significant hyperactivity or impulsive behaviors, such as interrupting others, blurting out answers, or feeling like you're 'on the go' all the time, and if these have been consistent or varied across different situations and over time?

Yes, my coworkers often joke that I'm always "on the go" and never stop moving, and I frequently catch myself interrupting people mid-sentence in meetings or jumping into their tasks. This restlessness and impulsivity have been a consistent pattern since childhood, as even my elementary school teachers noted that I blurted out answers and couldn't sit still.

Can you compare the severity of your symptoms between your current work environment and your previous work setup, focusing on how the shift from project-based work to high-volume demands has specifically affected your ability to manage your attention, organization, and impulsivity?

Under my previous project-based setup, I managed much better because it allowed me to do deep-focus troubleshooting and late-night tinkering at my own pace. However, the shift to a high-volume, rapid-response model with constant context-switching and strict metrics completely overwhelmed my attention and organization. This led to missed details and forgotten follow-ups, culminating in the major configuration mistake that put me on my current performance plan.

Can you describe any situations where you feel like you're able to control your hyperactivity and impulsivity, such as during hobbies or specific tasks, and if so, what makes those situations different from your daily work or school tasks?

I used to find a real sense of flow and focus during hands-on, deep-focus troubleshooting and late-night tinkering projects where I could actively engage with a problem. However, with quiet hobbies like reading a book or watching a movie, I struggle significantly with restlessness; sitting still quietly feels so uncomfortable that I constantly have to get up or pause what I'm doing.

Can you think of any situations, perhaps outside of work or school, where you're able to maintain focus and control your hyperactivity and impulsivity for an extended period, and if so, what characteristics of those situations might be contributing to this ability?

Honestly, I can't think of many situations where I feel in control of my focus or restlessness right now. Even at home, trying to relax with a book or a movie is really difficult because I just feel too restless to sit still. I used to enjoy late-night tinkering, but lately, it feels like I can't find any quiet scenario where I'm actually in control.

Have you experienced significant symptoms of inattention or hyperactivity during situations where you're highly motivated or interested, such as in hobbies or personal projects, or are these symptoms present across all situations regardless of your level of interest?

While I really enjoy things like late-night tinkering, these symptoms are present across almost all situations. Even during relaxing activities I want to do, like reading a book or watching a movie, I find myself reading the same page over and over, constantly pausing, or feeling too restless to just sit quietly.

Can you elaborate on whether there are specific triggers or environments that exacerbate your hyperactivity and impulsivity, or if these symptoms remain relatively consistent across different settings and tasks?

My restlessness and impulsivity definitely worsen in structured, slow-paced, or quiet environments where I am forced to sit still or wait. During long metrics meetings, three-hour classes, or while waiting in lines, I feel a massive buildup of pent-up energy that makes me fidget constantly and feel highly impatient. Even trying to relax at home with a book feels uncomfortable, and I often catch myself interrupting colleagues during our work stand-ups.

Have you experienced significant difficulties with inattention, hyperactivity, or impulsivity in social situations or during leisure activities, and if so, how do these symptoms impact your relationships or daily functioning outside of work and school?

Yes, they definitely spill over into my personal life and leisure time. It's incredibly hard to relax with a book or a movie because I feel so uncomfortable sitting still and constantly have to get up. This has also strained things with my wife, who gets very frustrated because I always forget daily responsibilities like paying bills, calling the plumber, or confirming appointments.

Can you confirm whether your symptoms of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity have been consistently present across all settings, including work, school, and personal life, or if there are specific situations where these symptoms significantly improve or worsen?

Yes, these issues are definitely present across all areas of my life—work, school, and home—though they have gotten significantly worse recently. At work, the fast-paced environment makes my inattention and disorganization much worse, leading to critical mistakes, while sitting through long evening lectures causes my mind to drift and my restlessness to spike. It also impacts my personal life, with my wife being frustrated over forgotten bills and my inability to even sit quietly to watch a movie or read a book.
Can you describe any situations or activities where your hyperactivity and impulsivity seem to decrease or are less problematic, and what factors might contribute to this decrease?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I haven't noticed any specific situations where my restlessness or impulsivity actually decreases. Lately, it just feels pretty constant and really hard to switch off, no matter what I'm trying to do.

You've mentioned that your symptoms have been present since childhood but have worsened with the change in your work demands. Can you think of any period in your life, perhaps during adolescence or early adulthood, where you felt your symptoms were less severe or better managed, even if it was just for a short time?

I can't really recall a specific period in my youth or early adulthood where my symptoms were significantly better or well-managed. While I somehow managed to get by back then, the distractibility and restlessness have always been a constant background presence in my life. It just wasn't until recently, with all the new demands at work, that it became completely overwhelming.

You mentioned that your symptoms have been present since childhood, but can you clarify if you experienced any periods of significant improvement or if the symptoms have been consistently problematic throughout your life, perhaps with some variations in severity?

My symptoms have been present in some form since childhood, but their severity has definitely fluctuated over the years. I was able to manage my distractibility and restlessness much better in the past when my job allowed for deep-focus troubleshooting and late-night tinkering. They only became consistently and severely problematic over the last two years when my work shifted to this high-volume, rapid-response model.

Have you ever experienced a period where your hyperactivity and impulsivity significantly improved or were well-managed without any interventions, and if so, what factors do you think contributed to this improvement?

I don't recall any specific period where these symptoms significantly improved or were well-managed on their own. I've generally struggled with restlessness and distractibility in some form ever since I was a kid.

Are your symptoms of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity present in all settings, including both work and personal life, or are they primarily problematic in specific situations like work or school?

Yes, they are definitely present in multiple areas of my life, not just at work. While the high-volume environment at my job has brought things to a crisis point with a performance plan, I also struggle in my evening classes with losing focus and falling behind. At home, I'm constantly forgetting bills and chores, and I can't even sit still to relax with a book or movie.

Can you think of any aspects of your life where you feel your symptoms of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity are less severe or more manageable, even if it's just for a short period, and what might be different about those situations?

I feel much more in control and focused when I am doing deep-focus troubleshooting on a single complex issue or tinkering with technology late at night on my own. When I don't have to constantly switch contexts, manage a rapid-fire queue, or deal with frequent interruptions, my symptoms feel much more manageable.

Can you clarify if your symptoms of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity are equally severe in all settings, or if they tend to worsen in specific situations, such as at work or in quiet environments?

No, they aren't equally severe everywhere, but they definitely worsen in specific situations. They are much worse at work now with the constant context-switching and distractions of the high-volume queue. At the same time, quiet or slow environments like my long evening classes, meetings, or even trying to read a book at home trigger intense restlessness and make it incredibly hard to focus.

Can you compare the severity of your symptoms between your most and least demanding tasks or environments, and how do you think the level of demand or structure affects your ability to manage your attention and restlessness?

My symptoms are at their absolute worst in the high-volume, rapid-response queue where the pressure to multitask causes me to make careless detail errors and get easily distracted. In passive, structured settings like long meetings or evening classes, I quickly lose focus after ten minutes and feel an intense, restless urge to get up and pace. In contrast, I feel much more in control during my late-night tinkering or old project-based work, where I can dive into deep-focus troubleshooting without the constant context-switching.

You've mentioned that your symptoms are worse in certain situations like high-volume work environments and quiet settings, but can you think of any specific factors or accommodations that have helped you manage your symptoms better in the past, such as structure, flexibility, or environmental changes?

I haven't really had any formal accommodations or specific strategies in the past. The only thing that seemed to help was working late at night when everything was much quieter, but other than that, I'm not really sure of any specific factors.

Can you describe any specific differences in how your symptoms of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity manifest in work settings versus social or leisure settings, and whether any settings significantly exacerbate or alleviate these symptoms?

At work, the high-volume, rapid-response setup really worsens my symptoms, causing me to miss details on tickets, get distracted by notifications, fidget on calls, and interrupt colleagues during meetings. In contrast, in leisure or home settings, it manifests as forgetting chores like paying bills, being unable to sit quietly to read a book or watch a movie without getting up, and feeling extremely impatient in lines.

Do you think your symptoms of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity are significantly impacting your daily life and relationships to the point where they are causing substantial distress or impairment in social, occupational, or other areas of functioning?

Yes, they are causing a huge amount of distress and have really disrupted my life across the board. At work, my disorganization led to a critical configuration mistake that hurt a major client and put me on a formal performance improvement plan. It's also hurting my personal life, as my evening class grades are slipping from missed assignments, and my wife is constantly frustrated with me for forgetting bills and household errands.

Have you ever experienced any periods where your symptoms of hyperactivity and impulsivity seemed to diminish or were less problematic without any specific interventions, and if so, what might have contributed to this change?

I don't really recall any periods where my restlessness or impulsivity went away or improved on their own. I've struggled with these symptoms in some form ever since I was a kid, so they've always been a constant presence.

Can you describe how your hyperactivity manifests in your daily adult life, particularly in situations that do not involve work or school, and if it has caused any significant problems in your personal relationships or daily functioning?

Outside of work and school, my restlessness makes it very hard to just relax at home; I can't sit quietly to read a book or watch a movie without constantly needing to get up because sitting still feels so uncomfortable. I also get extremely impatient and fidgety in everyday situations, like shifting around and getting irritated just waiting in line at a coffee shop.

Can you specify whether your symptoms of inattention, hyperactivity, and impulsivity have been consistently problematic across all settings since childhood, or if there were periods where they seemed less severe, particularly in comparison between your current work environment and past experiences?

While I've struggled with distractibility and restlessness since childhood—with teachers noting my daydreaming and inability to sit still—the symptoms were much less problematic in my past work setup of longer, project-based tasks where I could focus deeply. They only became severely impairing over the last two years when my job shifted to a high-volume, rapid-response model. This new environment, with its constant context-switching, completely overwhelmed my ability to manage my attention and organization.

Have you ever been diagnosed with or treated for any other psychiatric conditions, such as depression, anxiety, or substance use disorders, that might be contributing to or complicating your current symptoms?

No, I have never been diagnosed with or treated for any other psychiatric conditions, such as depression, anxiety, or substance use disorders. This is actually the first time I've ever sought out a psychiatric evaluation.
